newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia 97 grain output seen 71-76 mln T.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia 97 grain output seen 71-76 mln T.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an
independent research organisation specialising in agricultural
production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA 1997 GRAIN OUTPUT FORECAST AT 71-76 MILLION TONNES
MOSCOW, July 17 - Russia's total net grain output is forecast to be between 71 and 76 million tonnes, 5.0-6.0 percent higher than last year.

But estimates are only tentative at this early stage, particularly for spring grains sown in the Urals and Siberia. The final outcome will crucially depend on weather conditions until the beginning of large-scale harvesting in September.
Despite a decline in winter grain plantings, Russian farmers have maintained a total grain area at last year's level due to increase in spring grain plantings.

Most surplus grain producing areas have increased grain acreage, particularly in Povolzhsk and the North Caucasus. At the same time, all net grain consuming areas, especially North, North-West, Central, have reduced grain planted area.
Due to the likely increase in grain demand and supply, domestic grain trade in 1997/98 may intensify.

Though some areas (the extreme southern parts of Western Siberia, eastern part of the North Caucasus) have suffered from hot and dry weather, growing conditions remain generally favourable in most regions, particularly for winter grains in Central Chernozem (the Black Earth) and the North Caucasus.
As a result, grain yields are forecast to increase on last year in most areas.
While yields' forecasts for West and East Siberia remain tentative, early spring grain sowing, especially wheat, may result in higher yields due to reduced losses during the harvesting.
